To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“a signaling cascade is a retroactive device if the forward signaling is impeded”.

(a) there is an opposition in the parameter space between parameter sets favorizing forward and retro-signals; (b) there is a region of parameters where the cascade can act both as a forward and as a retro-signaler.

the direction of signal propagation is determined by the ratio of the total concentration of the phosphatase to that of the kinase, and the ratio of the Michaelis-Mentens constant of the kinase to that of the phosphatases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the control of signaling cascades by the biochemical parameters.
the conditions on biochemical parameter sets that can favor one or the others direction of signaling in a signaling cascade.
the identification of conditions on parameters which can be used to design signaling cascades with a specific behavior, in particular for the purpose of designing a retroactive device.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the forward signaling regime and the retro-signaling regime are not mutually exclusive, but rather that the former is the rule and the latter the exception, which can nevertheless be exploited to develop new signaling devices.
, depending on the biochemical parameters, a signaling cascade can be efficient in either one of the two directions of propagation, but not both simultaneously.
the direction of propagation is determined by a delicate balance of the biochemical parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the direction of signal propagation along a signaling cascade is a function of its biochemical properties.

the biochemical parameters of a signaling cascade are able to control the direction of information transmission, and that the forward or retro-signalling regimes can be favored or hindered by the values of these parameters.
the biochemical parameters of a cascade can be tuned in order to enhance a desired direction of propagation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the case of a signaling cascade, it is important to consider the possibility that a perturbation propagates upstream, and that this phenomenon can be favored or impeded by tuning the biochemical parameters.
the biochemical parameters can be used to design signaling cascades which can be either retroactive or non-interactive, depending on the application.
a given signaling cascade may be able to transmit information both in the forward direction and the retro direction, depending on the biochemical parameter set.
